transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-15
Start time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Omar Singh (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Maya Alvarez (Sable - Head of Procurement), Dr. Rajesh Kumar (Sable CTO), Evan Price (Sable Legal), Jonas Li (SRE)

Summary (auto): Procurement/legal review of MSA and DPA; SLA expectations clarified; Redwood to provide security artifacts and onboarding docs; schedule technical ramp.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena from Redwood - I'm here with Omar, our SE, and Priya from CSM. Can I do a quick roll call?
[00:10] Maya (Sable): Maya here, thanks.
[00:12] Rajesh (Sable CTO): Rajesh on the line.
[00:14] Evan (Legal): Evan here.
[00:16] Jonas (SRE): Jonas, hi.
[00:20] Lena: Great. Objective for today: walk through the MSA and DPA redlines we typically see, answer questions on SLAs (uptime, latency), chat about deployment modes - hosted vs dedicated vs private - and next steps for procurement and security.
[00:32] Maya: Perfect. We're mostly here to understand any sticky legal bits and confirm we can meet our security posture. Also pricing governance - our finance needs a clear pilot price and commit thresholds.
[00:45] Lena: Totally. Omar, do you want to start with the technical guarantees and how we typically put SLAs together?
[00:50] Omar (Redwood SE): Sure. So for hosted API we offer a standard SLA for availability - it's generally a 99.x number for the control plane; for strict enterprise contracts and Dedicated we can negotiate 99.9 and agreed p95/p99 latency targets depending on model and sequence lengths. Note, latency targets depend on model family and config, e.g., large-context LLMs at high concurrency will have different numbers.
[01:18] Rajesh: Can you call out what p95 numbers look like for heavy generation? We're doing clinical summarization and 1-2k token contexts sometimes.
[01:26] Omar: For 1-2k context on a quantized LLM on Dedicated infra we typically see p95 of 300-600 ms per token for streaming or a wall time of 600-1200 ms for 512-token responses - this varies. For hosted customers we publish performance profiles; for an SLA we'd pin a model and profile in the annex.
[01:48] Jonas: Important for us is predictable tail latency, especially during day batch jobs and peak hours. Do you do soft and hard throttles?
[01:55] Omar: Yes - we have rate limiting and quota tiers and can configure burst capacity. For Dedicated we also offer reserved GPU pools to avoid noisy neighbor effects. There's also smart routing and autoscaling options.
[02:10] Maya: On the legal side, Evan - you'll want to see data residency and DPA specifics. Lena, what does your DPA say about data retention and deletion?
[02:20] Lena: Our standard DPA states we process customer data only to provide the service, we retain logs for X days by default - we can configure retention, and for enterprise we provide options to reduce retention windows or provide S3 export and auto-delete. We also support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in Private deployments.
[02:40] Evan: Two questions: one, we need the DPA to reflect that Redwood will not use customer prompts for model training. Two, we need details on audit logs and access controls (RBAC).
[02:50] Omar: We have a section that covers model training, and for enterprise customers we can agree in writing that prompts are not used for training. Audit logs are available via the Console with token-level traces and can stream to your SIEM. RBAC and SSO/SAML are supported.
[03:12] Evan: Okay, good. Also any SOC 2 and ISO27001 evidence? We need to attach artifacts to the procurement packet.
[03:18] Priya (Redwood CSM): I'll share the SOC2 and ISO27001 certs and the summary of our security controls - we can also provide a redacted SOC2 report under NDA.
[03:27] Maya: Great. About the MSA - we have standard redlines around indemnity and limitation of liability, and we sometimes need a mutual indemnity clause for data breaches. Are you open to mutual indemnity?
[03:40] Lena: We generally have a limited liability clause but can discuss carveouts. For cyber incidents caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct we accept liability up to a defined cap; I'd need to confirm specifics with legal. We can take your redlines and come back.
[03:55] Evan: We'll send our preferred language. Also SLA credits - we need a defined credit mechanism rather than case-by-case.
[04:03] Lena: Understood. For Enterprise SLA annex we usually define a credit schedule tied to monthly uptime percentage and have thresholds and max credits. We'll include that template in the MSA package.
[04:15] Rajesh: Back to deployment question - we are leaning to Dedicated or Private because of PHI concerns. Can you summarize the differences?
[04:24] Omar: Sure - Hosted: fastest time-to-value, shared infrastructure, and standard controls - good for non-PHI use. Dedicated: isolated GPU pools in our infra with reserved capacity, better predictability, and stricter tenancy. Private: control plane is in your VPC or on-prem; customer-managed keys; ideal for regulated PHI use - we'd work through network setup (VPC peering, private endpoints).
[04:48] Jonas: For Private, do you support on-prem air-gapped deployments? We may need to run in a fully private cluster for some workloads.
[04:55] Omar: Yes - we offer an on-prem package; that has additional operational overhead and is typically an enterprise engagement. We can share the runbook for that.
[05:06] Maya: Cost - procurement will need a clear pilot price and the escalation path to production. Any standard pilot terms?
[05:14] Lena: Pilots are typically a 30-90 day evaluation with capped usage; we can offer a pilot price and then a committed monthly amount for Dedicated or private. We'll put together a pricing grid showing per-token/embedding rates, and uplift for Dedicated or Private.
[05:30] Rajesh: If we do Dedicated, are there commit minimums or hardware reservations?
[05:34] Lena: Yes, Dedicated generally includes a reserved capacity commitment - the size varies by throughput needs. We can propose a preliminary commit based on your projected QPS and token volume.
[05:44] Evan: Regarding security, can you describe key management - do you support BYOK (bring your own key)?
[05:50] Omar: For Private deployments yes, BYOK via KMS/HSM is supported. For Dedicated we offer customer-managed keys for specific attachments; hosted has our managed keys but we can discuss limited BYOK for enterprise deals.
[06:05] Jonas: How do you handle KV cache and session data - anything kept longer than a request window that might be an issue?
[06:12] Omar: We have automatic per-prefix KV caching to improve throughput; by default ephemeral caches live only for the session, and logs are separate. We can configure cache eviction and retention policies per customer for enterprise plans.
[06:28] Maya: Timeline: our procurement needs to complete vendor questionnaires and legal sign-off within three weeks if possible. Is that realistic?
[06:35] Lena: Yes, provided we get redlines quickly. We can aim to have documents back in 48 hours for initial redline review, SOC2 artifacts within a few days, and a technical ramp call scheduled within the week.
[06:48] Evan: We'll circulate our redlines once we get the doc - expect to have comments within two business days.
[06:52] Lena: Great. Omar - can you walk through the network onboarding steps for Private/VPC peering?
[06:58] Omar: Sure. For VPC peering we'll need an IP allowlist, peering CIDRs, and either AWS cross-account roles or peering configs depending on provider. We'll provide a network diagram, required ports (HTTPS and optional ports for telemetry), and our certificate thumbprints for mutual TLS. For on-prem there's an agent or appliance model.
[07:23] Jonas: Any hard constraints on IP ranges? We use some internal RFC1918 ranges - hope those are fine.
[07:28] Omar: RFC1918 is fine; we'll just need the exact subnets for routing.
[07:33] Maya: On pricing approvals - finance may need an exec signoff for any > $X threshold. We'll share thresholds offline. For now, can you send the pilot pricing and the committed pricing tiers?
[07:45] Priya: I'll put together a pricing grid that shows hosted vs dedicated vs private, including pilot discounts and ramp pricing. It will also show any setup fees.
[07:55] Evan: One more legal note - we need visibility into personnel access - for example, who at Redwood can access production logs and under what circumstances.
[08:05] Omar: We have role-based access with approvals for elevated access. We can provide a list of roles, and for enterprise customers we can do strict break-glass procedures with audit logging.
[08:18] Lena: We'll include that in the security packet.
[08:21] Maya: Are there any vendor onboarding forms you need from us? We have a standard questionnaire and an infosec checklist.
[08:28] Priya: Send them over and I'll complete the vendor side items. If there are any additional questions I'll follow up.
[08:34] Maya: Okay sending after the call.
[08:36] Lena: Quick note about crediting SLA violations - do you have a preferred remedy in the MSA?
[08:41] Evan: Credits are fine but we want a clear calculator.
[08:44] Lena: We'll include a credit table that maps monthly uptime percent to credits as a percentage of monthly fees.
[08:50] Rajesh: I want to flag performance testing - before we commit we want to run a short benchmark: 10k requests, a few concurrency patterns, to validate tail latency. Can Redwood support that?
[08:58] Omar: Absolutely. We can set up a private benchmark with pinned model version, and we can provide a config for load generator and a shared spreadsheet to capture p50/p95/p99. We may need a short Dedicated trial for that to be realistic.
[09:12] Jonas: Can you support CSM-led onboarding with runbook access?
[09:16] Priya: Yes. We'll provide an onboarding runbook, Slack channel, and weekly check-ins until handover.
[09:22] Maya: Good. Any compliance exceptions we should be aware of?
[09:25] Omar: No unusual ones - PHI requires Private or a compliant Dedicated with proper DPA terms and audit controls. We can map controls to HITRUST if needed but that's an advanced engagement.
[09:40] Evan: What about data deletion SLA? We need a guarantee that upon contract termination all customer data is deleted within 30 days.
[09:49] Lena: Standard is deletion within 30 days; for certain archives or backups we can also provide attestations. We'll add that to the DPA.
[09:57] Maya: Great. For the pilot, can you offer a month-to-month pricing with a cap and then a conversion to committed monthly for Dedicated?
[10:05] Lena: Yep - pilot pricing month-to-month with a clear conversion path is standard. We'll include an example pricing table as part of the proposal.
[10:12] Rajesh: One operational ask - can we get token-level cost attribution per team so our product folks can track cost?
[10:18] Priya: We have per-token cost reporting in the Console and can export usage by token, route, and model. We can also set up cost allocation tags.
[10:28] Jonas: Any E2E encryption in transit and at rest?
[10:31] Omar: TLS in transit; at rest we encrypt using keys - for Private you can use customer-managed keys.
[10:36] Evan: We need to review personnel background check standards for those with access to logs containing PHI.
[10:41] Lena: We'll include a personnel access summary and can discuss more in an HR/infosec call.
[10:46] Maya: Ok, nearing schedule here - can we agree next steps? I'll summarize then. Evan, legal will send redlines; Rajesh and Jonas will list technical constraints; procurement will need SOC2/ISO; Redwood sends MSA/DPA and pricing. Is that accurate?
[10:58] Evan: Yes.
[11:00] Rajesh: Yes.
[11:02] Lena: Correct. So action items - we will send docs and schedule the tech ramp call for 8/20. Priya will follow up with onboarding materials.
[11:12] Jonas: Works for us.
[11:15] Maya: We aim to finish procurement in three weeks if there are no big redlines.
[11:21] Lena: OK. Anything else?
[11:25] Evan: One minor point - can you confirm export formats for logs (syslog, S3)?
[11:30] Omar: Syslog, S3, and streaming to your SIEM are supported.
[11:34] Lena: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
[11:38] End of call notes: next steps and owners captured in action_items.
